rv.q: The result is—how you say?—exquisite.
"English" very rightfully won the Pulitzer Prize for Drama in 2023, and it's hands down a masterpiece of theater.
The exquisite Broadway production from director Knud Adams is the first must-see play of the season, and its lessons are likely to stick.
English arrives on Broadway like a welcome guest, a hopeful presence in a moment that feels like a particularly dismal party.
There's a ton of intelligence at work in 'English.'

A delicate, buoyant comedy about a small group of adults studying the language of the title, the play disarms and delights with its depiction of ordinary Iranian citizens seeking with determination to expand the horizons of their lives.
To speak in English in order to function in a new place, the play argues, forces non-native speakers to live forever in that gap.
Sanaz Toossi's stunning Broadway debut, is a precise study of language's significance.

Toossi has described “English” as her “scream into the void.” The actual show, then, is a surprise: a gentle, subtle experience that calibrates our ears to shifts in pedagogy and understanding. “English” débuted at the Atlantic, in a co-production with the Roundabout, in 2022.
Book a ticket right now—an exquisitely written, beautifully acted and mounted one hour and forty-five minutes of theater awaits.

Absolutely nothing gets lost in the translation of Sanaz Toossi’s English as the Pulitzer Prize-winning play about a group of Iranians longing for the West finally makes its Broadway debut, two years after its Off Broadway bow garnered critical raves and regional stagings won over audiences with its unfailing wit, grace and compassion.
Everything about this production is strikingly beautiful.
With its Broadway transfer, English seems to have found a universal language.
Because the performances are so strong, the cast members are able to mine English for every nuance of humor and individuality that is available to them.
It just doesn’t feel as deep as it did in 2022.
Overall, “English” is a heartfelt, honest, and witty play.
With empathy in short supply these days, English is a welcome reminder of what it feels like.

The universality of this idea and the passage of time as characters started to develop strong feelings about what learning English meant to them on a personal level was brilliantly conveyed through the lighting design.
English is an absorbing snapshot of people in transition, seeking reinvention and self-improvement while worrying if they will shed too much of what makes them themselves.
Toossi's oh-so-smart, Pulitzer Prize-winning play 'English' proves effective enough to raise its complex topics.
